title: Staff member reported a newsletter as suspicious

verdict.executive_summary: A low-severity user-reported phish alert was generated at 2026-08-29T08:31:00Z because Maryam Iqbal reported a newsletter from newsletter@marketwatchdaily.example as suspicious. Available evidence indicates this was a legitimate subscribed marketing email sent from an established benign sender to 62 recipients, with no attachment, a benign link, and no clicks or replies. This matters only as a triage decision: there is no indication of malicious email activity requiring Tier 2 review.
verdict.rationale: This alert type has a playbook entry and was triaged under Playbook §6 for user-reported phishing. The detection itself only proves that a user pressed the Report Phishing button, not that the message was malicious. The reported message came from a sender with a three-year incident-free history, passed sender authentication checks, matched prior harmless reports of the same sender, contained no attachment, and linked only to a normal marketing page. Mail logs show nobody clicked or replied, the message was distributed to 62 recipients as a normal subscription, threat intelligence on marketwatchdaily.example is benign across all configured feeds, baseline comparison shows no deviation, and there are no related alerts. The specific innocent explanation is that Maryam Iqbal did not recognise a legitimate newsletter sender and reported a benign subscription email; the deciding fact is whether the message was in fact a legitimate subscribed newsletter from the real sender, and the obtained evidence supports that innocent explanation. No hard trigger applies, all required enrichment sources answered, the user is not privileged or VIP, and the asset is low criticality and not a crown jewel. Because the rule fired on a user action rather than malicious activity, this is best classified as a False Positive for the alert, with close kind False positive.
verdict.claim_restated: The rule claims that Maryam Iqbal reported an email as suspicious by pressing the Report Phishing button.
clean_findings: Sender newsletter@marketwatchdaily.example has been emailing the company for three years without incident.
All three sender-identity checks passed, indicating the email authenticated as the claimed sender.
The only URL observed was https://marketwatchdaily.example/reports/q3-benchmark and it was described as a normal marketing page with nothing to fill in.
The same newsletter was delivered to 62 internal recipients as a normal subscription.
Mail logs confirm nobody clicked the link.
Mail logs confirm nobody replied to the message.
This exact sender has been reported six times before and each prior case was found harmless.
Threat intelligence from Feed A, Feed B, and Feed C all rate marketwatchdaily.example as benign.
Behavioural baseline comparison found no deviations on any measured dimension.
No related alerts were found sharing entities or infrastructure in the correlation window.
User m.iqbal@northbank.example is a standard user with low sign-in risk and no privileged or VIP status.
Host NB-RES-045 is low business criticality, managed, current on patches, and has healthy EDR.
verdict.innocent_explanation: Maryam Iqbal received a legitimate subscribed MarketWatch Daily newsletter, did not recognise the sender name, and used the Report Phishing button out of caution. This is supported by the sender's three-year benign history, passing sender-authentication checks, the absence of attachments, the benign marketing URL, delivery to 62 recipients as a normal subscription, no clicks or replies, and six prior harmless reports for the same sender/template.
verdict.malicious_explanation: An attacker could have sent a phishing email from infrastructure that appears legitimate, using a real-looking newsletter domain and authenticated sender to build trust before later credential harvesting or brand abuse. This would be supported by spoofing or compromised sender infrastructure, a malicious landing page, user interaction such as clicks or replies, targeting patterns inconsistent with normal subscriptions, or related alerts on the same sender or domain.
verdict.deciding_fact: Whether this specific message was a legitimate subscribed newsletter from the genuine marketwatchdaily.example sender rather than a phishing email impersonating it.
verdict.containment_considered: No containment was taken. Quarantining or blocking the sender/domain was considered unnecessary because evidence supports a legitimate marketing newsletter, nobody clicked or replied, no hard trigger fired, and Tier 1 should not disrupt benign business email without cause.

reasoning_chain.hypothesis: The alert is only evidence of a user report, not of malicious email activity.
evidence_for: Detection rule fires whenever an employee reports an email.
Rule description explicitly states it tells us nothing about whether the email is actually dangerous.
reasoning_chain.conclusion: The alert must be evaluated on message context; the report action alone is not suspicious enough to escalate.

reasoning_chain.hypothesis: The reported email is a legitimate newsletter or marketing message.
evidence_for: Sender has emailed the company for three years without incident.
The only link was to a normal marketing page with nothing to fill in.
The same newsletter went to 62 people as a normal subscription.
Same sender was reported six times before and each case was harmless.
Threat intelligence across all configured feeds is benign.
evidence_against: The message was reported as suspicious by the recipient.
Recipient stated they did not recognise the sender name.
reasoning_chain.conclusion: Strongly supported; the report is consistent with user caution rather than malicious email.

reasoning_chain.hypothesis: The email is a phishing attempt that should be escalated.
evidence_for: Any unsolicited email with a link can theoretically be phishing.
evidence_against: Authenticated sender with long benign history.
No attachment and no credential collection page indicated.
Broad normal-recipient distribution rather than targeted lure.
No clicks, replies, related alerts, or behavioural deviations.
No finance or executive targeting and no spoofed internal/partner domain.
reasoning_chain.conclusion: Not supported by available evidence; malicious explanation cannot compete with the benign explanation here.

recommended_next_steps: Close the alert as False positive because the detection captured a user report of a legitimate newsletter rather than malicious email activity.
Optionally provide user-awareness feedback to Maryam Iqbal that the reported message was a legitimate subscription newsletter.
